decisions.rationale: Verified. The page python/fastapi-services/calling-the-spring-boot-api-from-fastapi-service-url-token-and-timeouts/artifact.md teaches 502 for a refused connection (line 15 'commonly 504 for a timeout and 502 for other upstream failures'; cheat-sheet line 86 'Refused connection | ConnectError | 502'; explore model line 109) and its graded editor fails 'Use 502 for a connection failure.' (artifact.html:543). The lab dictates 503 (README:110, README:161, starter upstream.py docstring line 32) and test_main.py:154 enforces it. Probe (review/l3-recon/probes/upstream_502.py and upstream_pageidiom502.py over my own scratch solution): 1 failed, 9 passed, 'Task 6: expected UpstreamError(503, ...), got UpstreamError(502, ...)'. The page is the source of truth and is not technically wrong (502 is the conventional gateway answer, as both critics note). Required fix: 502 with detail 'Workshop service unavailable' in README:110, test_main.py:154 (and its message), the upstream.py docstring, and README:161 ('the route answers 502'). Same decision as py-api-lab-sme-005. Task 6 target (one coherent fix for edu-001, sme-005, edu-004, sme-004, sme-010): README Task 6 teaches the page recipe (inside try: response = client.get(...); response.raise_for_status(); except httpx.TimeoutException -> UpstreamError(504, 'Workshop service timed out'); except httpx.TransportError -> UpstreamError(502, 'Workshop service unavailable'); except httpx.HTTPStatusError as err -> UpstreamError(502, f'Workshop service returned {err.response.status_code}')); test_task06 expects 502 for ConnectError and adds a ConnectTimeout case expecting (504, 'Workshop service timed out'); both the raise_for_status idiom and an is_success check, and both a TransportError and a ConnectError catch, must still pass (the page's graded editor, artifact.html:536/542, accepts ConnectError in place of TransportError, so no ReadError case is required).

Verified. MUTANTS['fetch_workshop never raises'] (test_main.py:205) rebinds only signups_api.upstream.fetch_workshop, but starter main.py:11 imports the name and run_learner_tests imports main first (test_main.py:212-214), so the route keeps the real function. Probe review/l3-recon/probes/test_routelevel.py (404 test with override + route-level test overriding get_workshop_client with an httpx.MockTransport raising ReadTimeout, asserting 504): 1 failed, 9 passed with the false message 'your tests still pass when fetch_workshop never raises'. Required fix: patch both bindings, 'u.fetch_workshop = m.fetch_workshop = ...' (verified in scratch probes/test_main_fixed.py: route-level suite then passes 10/10, README-style suite still passes). Optionally say in Task 8 that a route-level test through get_workshop_client is also accepted. Same decision as py-api-lab-sme-002.

Verified. serving#o3 is claimed (lab.json:15) but Task 8 only checks the substring 'dependency_overrides' (test_main.py:229), and neither mutant needs an override to be killed. Probe review/l3-recon/probes/test_nooverride.py (dependency_overrides.clear() then GET /signups/999 against the real fixture, plus fetch_workshop(None, 7) under pytest.raises(Exception)) passes 10/10. The 'provide ... to routes as a dependency' half IS observed: the Task 1-3 and 7 checks override get_repository with SIGNUPS that differ from fixtures/signups.json, so only a route that takes repo=Depends(get_repository) passes; no learner-written provider is required. The 'replace it in tests with a dependency override' half is not observed. Required fix: make Task 8 observe an override doing work. A full-repository must-still-pass run alone is NOT sufficient: my prototype (probes/test_main_fixed.py, swap run with ids 1-1000) catches test_nooverride.py but test_422only.py (no override, asserts GET /signups/abc is 422) still passes 10/10. Suggested mechanism: an AST check for an assignment whose target is a Subscript of an attribute named dependency_overrides (keyed by get_repository) plus the data-swap run, or recording the keys assigned into app.dependency_overrides during the learner run. Task 8 recheck outcomes: Task 8 must FAIL for a suite in which no test assigns a get_repository entry into app.dependency_overrides (probes test_nooverride.py and test_422only.py) and for a suite whose mock transport does no work (test_nonemock.py: an unused MockTransport plus pytest.raises(Exception) around fetch_workshop(None, 7)); Task 8 must PASS for the README-style suite, the route-level suite test_routelevel.py and, once sme-009 is fixed, the class-based suite test_class.py. Also update README:129 and the lab.json notes so they describe the new Task 8 runs. Dropping the claim is not an accepted alternative here: the fix is cheap and the technique is the module's core testing lesson. Merged with py-api-lab-sme-001 (same required outcome).

Verified by reading. The page teaches raise_for_status() + HTTPStatusError and 'Catch TimeoutException before TransportError; the first matching except wins' (artifact.md:15, 32, 56, 87; editor steps artifact.html:354). README Task 6 (lines 105-111) dictates except ConnectError plus 'not response.is_success', which never practises the ordering lesson and never mentions raise_for_status; 'Translate every failure' is untrue (ReadError/RemoteProtocolError escape as 500). The page idiom with the page's status passes once the status is aligned (probe review/l3-recon/probes/upstream_pageidiom503.py: 10 passed). Required fix: README Task 6 teaches the page recipe and drops 'every' (even the page recipe lets a non-JSON 2xx body escape as a 500). Not required: the ReadError test case, because the page's own graded editor accepts a ConnectError catch in place of TransportError (artifact.html:536, 542) and the lab must not fail a solution the page grades correct; the existing ReadTimeout case already fails a learner who catches TransportError before TimeoutException. Task 6 target (one coherent fix for edu-001, sme-005, edu-004, sme-004, sme-010): README Task 6 teaches the page recipe (inside try: response = client.get(...); response.raise_for_status(); except httpx.TimeoutException -> UpstreamError(504, 'Workshop service timed out'); except httpx.TransportError -> UpstreamError(502, 'Workshop service unavailable'); except httpx.HTTPStatusError as err -> UpstreamError(502, f'Workshop service returned {err.response.status_code}')); test_task06 expects 502 for ConnectError and adds a ConnectTimeout case expecting (504, 'Workshop service timed out'); both the raise_for_status idiom and an is_success check, and both a TransportError and a ConnectError catch, must still pass (the page's graded editor, artifact.html:536/542, accepts ConnectError in place of TransportError, so no ReadError case is required).

Verified: README:87 marks the run 'Optional', no check runs the app, and the page teaches 'fastapi dev main.py' (fastapi-routes/artifact.md:15, 65) while starter/requirements.txt pins plain fastapi without fastapi-cli ('python -m fastapi --help' in the l3 venv fails). Decided consistently with py-api-lab-sme-003: the claim stays only if a test observes it, and a run cannot be observed without opening a socket, so the 'keep the claim with a note' option is not accepted. Required fix: (1) drop python/fastapi-services/fastapi-routes#o1 from lab.json objectives (keep the topic in covers) and record in lab.json notes that Tasks 1-3 practise and observe the route-definition clause while running the app locally stays with the page and the optional uvicorn step; (2) add one sentence at README:87 that the page's fastapi dev needs the fastapi[standard] extra, which this lab does not install, so python -m uvicorn signups_api.main:app starts the same app.

Verified in the shipped starter: test_task05 fails with a raw pydantic_core ValidationError '3 validation errors for Settings ... Extra inputs are not permitted' (test_main.py:121 builds Settings(...) with Task 4's fields), contradicting README:21 'Each failing check names its task and the next action'. The Task 1/2/3/7 route messages name the task but not the action ('must answer 201, got 404'). Required fix: decouple Task 5's check from Task 4 (e.g. a types.SimpleNamespace config with the three attributes) or turn the Settings failure into a 'Task 5: finish Task 4 first' message; and append the next action to the route-status messages (e.g. 'got 404: add the @app.post("/signups", ...) route'). The other raw-error states are decided under py-api-lab-sme-008.

Verified against python/data-pipelines/coding-lab: its fixtures hold chen.li.example.com (rejected by its Task 5 'email needs @', README:134) and Dana Kim seats 'two' (rejected, README:137), and Ana Ruiz's latest sign-up is session 'data' (signed 2026-11-03, kept by latest_per_email, README:141); this lab's fixtures/signups.json has Chen Li and Dana Kim as loaded and Ana Ruiz in 'general'. The serving page frames serving as read-only GET routes (serving artifact.md:13) while Task 1 adds POST /signups that lives only in memory. Required fix: (1) one framing sentence in the README Goal: the pipeline's export adds the desk's id, workshop and status, this lab reads a JSON snapshot of it, and POST /signups records a walk-in at the desk in this app's memory only (the pipeline stays the source of truth); (2) regenerate fixtures/signups.json so its people match the pipeline lab's accepted, deduplicated output (drop or correct Chen Li and Dana Kim, Ana Ruiz in 'data'). The lab checks use their own SIGNUPS (test_main.py:27), so no check changes. Splitting the POST into a separate resource is not required.

Verified: lab.json notes say the 45-minute median covers the eight tasks only, README:9 does not mention setup, and the README names no stopping point although S18 gives two coding-lab blocks (20 + 40 minutes); the sibling labs name one (data-pipelines README:80, python-fundamentals README:66). Required fix: say whether setup (venv + pip install) is inside or outside the estimate, name the block split and a natural stopping point (e.g. setup and Tasks 1-3 in the 20-minute block, Tasks 4-8 in the 40-minute block), keep the 60-minute cap sentence, and re-check the 45-minute estimate after the Task 6 and Task 8 changes from this reconciliation.

Verified: spring-boot/spring-boot-basics/coding-lab/starter/src/main/java/workshops/CatalogConfig.java seeds workshops 1 and 2 only, while fixtures/signups.json gives Dana Kim workshop_id 3; that lab's starter has no bearer-token check (no Authorization/token handling in its src or README). Required fix (scoped): (1) use workshop ids 1 and 2 only in fixtures/signups.json, or say id 3 is deliberately unknown (this may be resolved by the edu-007 fixture regeneration); (2) one sentence that the Basics-lab catalog ignores the token while a deployed catalog checks it. Not required: the optional Spring end-to-end step, which adds setup against the captain's minimal-setup rule.

The sibling Python module labs in this branch dictate at the same level: python/data-pipelines/coding-lab/README.md:94 gives the full SELECT and :100 the full UPSERT_SQL; python/python-fundamentals/coding-lab/README.md:97-98 and :132 spell out the loop, the comparisons and the waitlist=None fix. Withholding code only here would make this lab inconsistent with its siblings. The time budget is already tight (45-minute estimate against the 60-minute cap of the captain's 30-60 minute module lab, see edu-008), and this reconciliation adds Task 6 and Task 8 work, so adding unscaffolded decision points would push novices past the cap. The finding is a low-severity style preference, not a correctness or objective-observation defect.

Verified all three. (1) pytest -v on my scratch solution runs starter/test_api.py before tests/test_main.py, so expected/on-completion.txt ('........<one dot for each of your own tests>') has the order reversed; lab-contract 6 requires the completion summary to match expected/. (2) README:87 says 'From the starter folder' after README:33 opened the terminal in the lab folder, with no cd and no return. (3) README:79 states the return before the None check. Required fix: expected line '<one dot for each of your own tests>........'; give cd starter, the uvicorn command and cd .. before testing; reword Task 2 to look up, raise 404 when None, otherwise return.

Verified and merged with py-api-lab-edu-003. Probe review/l3-recon/probes/test_nonemock.py (override-based 404 test plus an unused httpx.MockTransport and pytest.raises(Exception) around fetch_workshop(None, 7)) passes 10/10 against the shipped checks, so calling#o3 (mock transport) is observed only as a substring (test_main.py:230); test_nooverride.py likewise passes, so serving#o3 is over-claimed. Required fix for the mock-transport half: patch both bindings (edu-002) and add a mutant that only a status-asserting test kills, e.g. fetch_workshop raising UpstreamError(500, 'wrong') (my prototype probes/test_main_fixed.py fails test_nonemock.py with 'your tests still pass when fetch_workshop answers every failure with the wrong status' while the README-style and route-level suites pass); replacing the 'MockTransport' substring with an AST check for an httpx.MockTransport(...) call is optional hardening (a hand-rolled fake client asserting 504 would still pass without it). Required fix for the override half: as in edu-003. Also update README:129 and the lab.json notes to describe the new Task 8 runs. Task 8 recheck outcomes: Task 8 must FAIL for a suite in which no test assigns a get_repository entry into app.dependency_overrides (probes test_nooverride.py and test_422only.py) and for a suite whose mock transport does no work (test_nonemock.py: an unused MockTransport plus pytest.raises(Exception) around fetch_workshop(None, 7)); Task 8 must PASS for the README-style suite, the route-level suite test_routelevel.py and, once sme-009 is fixed, the class-based suite test_class.py.

Same finding and decision as py-api-lab-edu-002 (verified: test_routelevel.py gives 1 failed, 9 passed with the false 'never raises' message). Required fix: 'u.fetch_workshop = m.fetch_workshop = ...' in the mutant; optionally say in README Task 8 that a route-level test through get_workshop_client is accepted.

Verified: fastapi-routes#o1 ('... and run the app locally') is claimed at lab.json:11 but the run is optional (README:87) and every check uses the in-process TestClient. Required fix (same as py-api-lab-edu-005): drop python/fastapi-services/fastapi-routes#o1 from lab.json objectives, keep the topic in covers, and record in lab.json notes that the route-definition clause is practised and observed by Tasks 1-3 while the run-locally clause stays with the page and the optional step. Do not add a socket-opening check. Splitting the objective in topic.json would be a page change and is not part of this fix.

Verified: probe review/l3-recon/probes/upstream_readtimeout_only.py (except httpx.ReadTimeout instead of TimeoutException) passes 10/10, so a ConnectTimeout, WriteTimeout or PoolTimeout would escape as a 500 and calling#o2's timeout clause is only partly observed. Required fix: add a ConnectTimeout case to test_task06 expecting (504, 'Workshop service timed out'). Task 6 target (one coherent fix for edu-001, sme-005, edu-004, sme-004, sme-010): README Task 6 teaches the page recipe (inside try: response = client.get(...); response.raise_for_status(); except httpx.TimeoutException -> UpstreamError(504, 'Workshop service timed out'); except httpx.TransportError -> UpstreamError(502, 'Workshop service unavailable'); except httpx.HTTPStatusError as err -> UpstreamError(502, f'Workshop service returned {err.response.status_code}')); test_task06 expects 502 for ConnectError and adds a ConnectTimeout case expecting (504, 'Workshop service timed out'); both the raise_for_status idiom and an is_success check, and both a TransportError and a ConnectError catch, must still pass (the page's graded editor, artifact.html:536/542, accepts ConnectError in place of TransportError, so no ReadError case is required).

Same finding and decision as py-api-lab-edu-001: align with the page's 502 for ConnectError (README:110, README:161, upstream.py docstring, test_main.py:154). Verified by probe upstream_502.py (fails Task 6 only on the status). Task 6 target (one coherent fix for edu-001, sme-005, edu-004, sme-004, sme-010): README Task 6 teaches the page recipe (inside try: response = client.get(...); response.raise_for_status(); except httpx.TimeoutException -> UpstreamError(504, 'Workshop service timed out'); except httpx.TransportError -> UpstreamError(502, 'Workshop service unavailable'); except httpx.HTTPStatusError as err -> UpstreamError(502, f'Workshop service returned {err.response.status_code}')); test_task06 expects 502 for ConnectError and adds a ConnectTimeout case expecting (504, 'Workshop service timed out'); both the raise_for_status idiom and an is_success check, and both a TransportError and a ConnectError catch, must still pass (the page's graded editor, artifact.html:536/542, accepts ConnectError in place of TransportError, so no ReadError case is required).

Task 5 half verified: with probe review/l3-recon/probes/upstream_notransport.py (make_client without transport=transport) and a getaddrinfo-blocking plugin (probes/plugins/blocknet.py), test_task05 attempts a DNS lookup for 'workshops.test' and fails with a raw httpx.ConnectError, so the 'Task 5: pass transport=transport' message (test_main.py:128) is unreachable and lab.json 'network.test: none' / the docstring 'No test opens a network connection' are untrue for wrong solutions; my correct solution under the same block passes 10/10. Task 7 half by inspection: test_task07's client fixture does not clear SPRING_*, so a route that builds make_client(Settings()) itself would use the learner's shell values. Required outcome (recheckable): with probes/upstream_notransport.py under probes/plugins/blocknet.py, test_task05 attempts no DNS lookup or connection and fails with the Task 5 transport message; a try/except around the request alone does not meet this, because the lookup still happens. One possible in-test mechanism (not run by me): before the request, make the real httpx transport unusable for the duration of the check (e.g. monkeypatch httpx.HTTPTransport.handle_request to fail with the Task 5 message). In the Task 7 checks, delenv SPRING_BASE_URL and SPRING_TOKEN. Prefer an in-test guard over a session-wide socket-blocking fixture, since tests/test_main.py should hold nothing but task checks.

Verified: the pinned FastAPI's fastapi/openapi/docs.py (l3 venv, lines 79 and 92) loads swagger-ui-bundle.js and swagger-ui.css from https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/swagger-ui-dist@5/, so README:147 'Only the setup step uses the network' is untrue for the README:87 /docs step; and 'fastapi dev' is not installed (see edu-005). Required fix: amend the Offline note (the /docs page needs the internet in the browser; offline, use curl or /openapi.json), add the fastapi dev vs uvicorn sentence once (shared with edu-005), and give the env-var commands in the README:161 troubleshooting entry (export ... on macOS/Linux, $env:... in PowerShell).

Verified: the shipped starter fails test_task05 with a raw pydantic ValidationError (see edu-006), and probe review/l3-recon/probes/settings_tokendefault.py (spring_token: str = '') fails test_task04 with 'Failed: DID NOT RAISE Exception' before the Task 4 message at test_main.py:111. A Task 7 route without try/except raises UpstreamError through TestClient (raise_server_exceptions defaults to True), so the Task 7 message is unreachable (by inspection). Required fix: give the Task 4 token check a Task 4 message (e.g. try/except around pytest.raises, or check the error without pytest.raises), the Task 5 decoupling from edu-006, and a Task 7 message for an uncaught UpstreamError (e.g. a TestClient with raise_server_exceptions=False for Task 7, or catching the exception into a pytest.fail); passing _env_file=None in the Task 4 check is optional. Softening README:21 to 'Most failing checks' is an accepted alternative only for whatever raw states remain after these fixes.

Verified: probe review/l3-recon/probes/test_class.py (the README's two tests as methods of class TestApi) fails Task 8 with 'add at least two test functions' / 'assert 0 >= 2' because test_main.py:226 counts only module-level FunctionDef nodes. Required fix: count test_* functions including methods of Test* classes (ast.walk), or count collected tests from the clean run.

Verified: README:105 'Translate every failure' is untrue (other TransportError subclasses escape as 500), and README:100 'a slow catalog cannot hold your request open' overstates httpx timeouts, which apply per operation (connect, read, write, pool), not as a total deadline. Required fix: drop 'every' (a non-JSON 2xx body still escapes even with the page recipe), teach the page's TransportError catch, and reword README:100 so the timeout bounds each step of the call.
